speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you were in a rear-end collision and are experiencing right groin pain with an abnormal leg position. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned, and are you able to move your toes or foot at all?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. You mentioned pain in both knees as well; can you tell me if your right leg is rotated outward (externally rotated) and shortened compared to the left side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The internal rotation and adduction of the leg strongly suggest a posterior hip dislocation rather than a fracture. Can you confirm if you have any numbness or tingling in your right leg, and are you able to actively extend your right knee against resistance?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to see the imaging to confirm the suspected posterior hip dislocation. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a posterior dislocation of the right hip, which aligns with the leg's internal rotation and adduction. I will now request images to better visualize the dislocation before finalizing the management plan. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of a shortened, internally rotated, and adducted leg following a high-energy mechanism like a rear-end collision is classic for posterior hip dislocation. The pelvic X-ray has confirmed this diagnosis by ruling out fractures and showing the abnormal alignment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
